description: Scottish setting, true life story of John Davidson. Diagnosed with Tourette's at 15, targeted as 'insane' by his peers, he struggled with a condition few had witnessed. Campaigning for better understanding and acceptance of the condition of Tourette's as an adult, he finds his life's purpose and accepted his MBE from the Queen in 2019.
critics_consensus: A deft balance of prickly and sweet that's bound together by Robert Aramayo's knockout performance, I Swear doesn't sugarcoat the challenges of Tourette syndrome while delivering an uplifting tale of resilience.

reviews.name: Matt Oakes
reviews.review: Kirk Jones’ biographical account of Tourette’s advocate John Davidson is a moving and often very funny drama that finds compassion in contradiction, anchored by a breakout performance from Robert Aramayo.

reviews.name: Matthew St. Clair
reviews.publication: Cinematic Words of a Chaotic Gemini (Substack)
reviews.review: A heart-rending vessel for understanding led by a lived-in leading performance from Robert Aramayo.

reviews.name: John Stark
reviews.review: Do yourself a favor and check out this heartwarming biopic. I swear you won’t regret it.

reviews.name: Joanna Langfield
reviews.review: This biography, ostensibly about one man’s sad journey with Tourette’s Syndrome, is also very much about enlightenment and compassion. And it just about wrecked me.

reviews.name: Ross McIndoe
reviews.review: Its mix of compassion and clarity allows it to avoid the easy sentimentality of similar tales.

reviews.name: Robin Clifford
reviews.review: Jones and his two stars – young and grown up John – do a fine job in showing how the syndrome can isolate and destroy the life of the victim.

reviews.name: Laura Clifford
reviews.review: it's not just Aramayo who impresses here...The movie, itself, though, falters, David Davidson's abandonment of his family coming out of nowhere and writer/director Kirk Jones embracing movie-of-the-week cliche in his final act.

reviews.name: Natasha Alvar
reviews.review: The film is tonally well-balanced. It’s equal parts moving and funny, and while darkness is part of the film’s discourse, it never overwhelms the narrative.

reviews.name: Luis Martínez
reviews.review: Kirk Jones crafts a drama about overcoming adversity and good feelings in the most conventional, orthodox, and irresistible of senses. [Full review in Spanish]

reviews.name: Dave Giannini
reviews.review: I Swear is approachable, enjoyable, and buoys your spirits.

reviews.name: Marta Medina Pérez
reviews.review: Although I Swear has a strong TV-movie vibe, it remains compelling thanks to a screenplay that strikes a balance between drama and comedy, and, above all, to Robert Aramayo, who delivers the performance of a lifetime. [Full Review in Spanish]

reviews.name: Belen Prieto
reviews.review: The film doesn't try to reinvent anything, it simply tells a story well, a story we needed to know. [Full review in Spanish]

reviews.name: Alex Maidy
reviews.review: Rich with vulnerability, Robert Aramayo delivers one of the most authentic and touching performances of the year in a movie that is impossible to dislike.

reviews.name: Santiago Alverú
reviews.review: Robert Aramayo transforms himself as only the best actors can, with a technique and a commitment to his craft so unwavering that it dispels any doubt about his dedication and respect. [Full review in Spanish]

reviews.name: Andrea Zamora
reviews.review: I Swear isn't just a film to be enjoyed; it's one from which you learn, one that holds up a mirror to your ignorance born of privilege, and that achieves the greatest thing cinema can do: create empathy. [Full review in Spanish]

reviews.name: Fran Chico
reviews.review: Its structure is unsurprisingly that of a typical biopic, but the film's greatest strength...lies in its ability to reflect the shift in perception that we experience alongside those around the protagonist. [Full review in Spanish]

reviews.name: Cameron Meier
reviews.review: It’s not every day a film changes your mind about something.

reviews.name: Jane Freebury
reviews.review: Robert Aramayo is astonishing as the Scottish disability campaigner, quiet and self-effacing one moment, wildly disruptive the next, then stricken with remorse

reviews.name: Ruth Maramis
reviews.review: A masterclass of inspirational storytelling that sheds light on Tourette’s syndrome. Robert Aramayo embodies John Davidson with deep vulnerability, grit, and a quiet grace, one of the best of the year so far.

reviews.name: Jake Wilson
reviews.review: ...[Robert Aramayo] and newcomer Scott Ellis Watson, who plays the young Davidson, have worked hard between them to make the John of the film a fully-fledged character rather than defining him by his tics.
